what: A drug screen with simulated data
title: Perturbation analysis of Cell Painting data with cellpaintr
text: generateData() simulates small CellProfiler table 1,000 cells six patients eight drugs, 10 shape, 10 intensity, 10 texture features named real CellProfiler output. Drugs D7 D8 shift texture features; D1 control. Every drug compared control, p-values comparisons feature groups adjusted together. quick screen many drugs, corrected t-test needs refits. p-values adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure drugs feature groups.
code: set.seed(23) sce_sim <- loadData(generateData()) sce_sim <- transformScale(sce_sim, robust = TRUE) sce_sim$Drug <- relevel(as.factor(sce_sim$Drug), ref = "D1") types_sim <- c("AreaShape", "Intensity", "Texture")  sce_list <- map(setdiff(levels(sce_sim$Drug), "D1"), function(drug) {     predictLOO(         sce_sim,         target = "Drug", group = "Patient",         interest_level = drug, reference_level = "D1",         types = types_sim, n_threads = 1, progress = FALSE     ) }) p_adj_cutoff <- 0.05 fc_cutoff <- 0.5 tb_stats <- lapply(sce_list, calculateStats,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient", method = "corrected" ) |>     bind_rows() |>     mutate(pvalue_adj = p.adjust(pvalue, method = "BH")) |>     mutate(Selection = ifelse(         pvalue_adj < p_adj_cutoff & log2FoldChange > fc_cutoff,         Target, ""     ))  tb_stats |>     ggplot(aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(pvalue_adj), label = Selection)) +     geom_vline(         xintercept = c(0, fc_cutoff), alpha = 0.5, linetype = "dashed"     ) +     geom_hline(         yintercept = c(0, -log10(p_adj_cutoff)), alpha = 0.5,         linetype = "dashed"     ) +     geom_point(aes(color = Target)) +     geom_text_repel(aes(color = Target), max.overlaps = Inf) +     xlab("log2 fold change") +     ylab("-log10 p-value (BH adjusted)") +     facet_wrap(~Feature) +     ggtitle(paste0("False discovery rate: ", 100 * p_adj_cutoff, "%"))

title: Test each feature group for a difference between two levels — calculateStats
code: set.seed(23) cell_file <- generateData() sce <- loadData(cell_file) sce <- transformScale(sce)  sce$Drug <- as.factor(sce$Drug) sce$Drug <- relevel(sce$Drug, ref = "D1")  sce_single <- predictLOO(     sce,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient",     interest_level = "D7", reference_level = "D1",     n_threads = 1 )  # permutation test; by default, it enumerates all 64 relabelings of the # six patients, here 9 random relabelings keep the example fast calculateStats(sce_single,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient",     n_permutations = 9 ) #> Permutation test with 10 relabelings of 6 levels of 'Patient' (paired design); smallest attainable p-value 1/10. #> 'P1' keeps its labels, because exchanging the two levels of 'Drug' in all levels of 'Patient' at once gives the same statistic. #>   Target Feature pvalue log2FoldChange #> 1     D7     all    0.1      0.9328005  # corrected t-test: no refits calculateStats(sce_single,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient",     method = "corrected" ) #>   Target Feature       pvalue log2FoldChange #> 1     D7     all 0.0001791293      0.9328005  # correction of Nadeau and Bengio: no refits, corrects less calculateStats(sce_single,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient",     method = "nadeau_bengio" ) #>   Target Feature       pvalue log2FoldChange #> 1     D7     all 0.0001322961      0.9328005  # p-values from the t-distribution: fast but anti-conservative calculateStats(sce_single,     target = "Drug", group = "Patient",     method = "t" ) #>   Target Feature       pvalue log2FoldChange #> 1     D7     all 1.971207e-05      0.9328005
